fields.Name: magnetmail
fields.Description: Higher Logic Marketing Enterprise (formerly Real Magnet/MagnetMail) — legacy SOAP/XML email-marketing platform (mmapi.asmx, 55 ops): recipients, groups, messages, tracking, unsubscribes, bulk-CSV uploads. Two-step session-token auth. No delete op exists.

Configuration.SoapActionPattern: http://www.magnetmail.net/{OperationName}  (exact match to the WSDL <s:element> operation name; e.g. http://www.magnetmail.net/getMessagesUTC)

AuthFlowDetail.step1: POST Authenticate(username, password) to the shared endpoint (no <mmAuthHeader> on this ONE call -- it has no soap:header binding, confirmed from the WSDL binding section).
AuthFlowDetail.step1Response: AuthenticateResponse.AuthenticateResult (type tns:AuthenticationResult) carries: authenticated (bool), sessionId (string), loginid (int), login_name (string), user_nbr (int), partition_id (int), is_parent_mail_user (int), parent_user_id (string), user_id (string).
AuthFlowDetail.step2: Every subsequent operation (all 54 others) carries a SOAP HEADER named mmAuthHeader (complexType tns:mmAuthHeader) with exactly two fields: sessionId (string) and user_id (string) -- both copied verbatim from step1's AuthenticationResult.sessionId / AuthenticationResult.user_id.
AuthFlowDetail.sessionExpiry: Not stated anywhere in the WSDL -- no TTL/expiry field on AuthenticationResult and no refresh-token operation exists. Provable-only: leave session lifetime unasserted.

PaginationDefaults.note: No single vendor-wide pagination convention. Per-operation param names verified directly against the WSDL request-element definitions; pick the exact convention per operation, never assume.

conventions.style: NO pagination -- confirmed no pageNo/PageNo/pageNumber/page-family field anywhere in the operation request element or its nested criteria type
operations: SearchPersonifySubscriptionMappings (criteria tns:PersonifySubscriptionMappingSearchCriteria extends tns:DomainBase, which is empty -- no paging fields)
(remaining single-record / mutation / send operations take no pagination by construction)

getMessagesUTC.note: getMessagesUTC ALSO exposes a second, independent date-range (createStartDate/createEndDate) on the message CREATE date -- do not conflate the two; the SENT range is the incremental-sync-relevant watermark.

otherObservedConventions.note: snake_case -- distinct from every other convention observed

IncrementalWatermark.vendorWideConclusion: At least 5 distinct from/to date-range param-name conventions coexist across the operation surface -- never assume a single vendor-wide name; verify per-operation against the WSDL request element.

COMPLEX_WRAPPERS.note: 6 of 55 operations wrap their filter/search parameters in a single <criteria> child element instead of flat top-level params. Confirmed directly from each request s:element definition.

ErrorResponseShape.note: Mutation/action response wrapper types (SaveResult, EmailToIndividualResult, EmailToGroupResult, UploadListResult, ...) each carry an in-band error signal INSIDE the 200/literal SOAP body -- confirmed on 4+ distinct response complexTypes. A caller must check this field even on a structurally successful SOAP response; a SOAP Fault is not the only failure signal this API uses.

fields.error: s:double, nillable -- numeric error flag (0 = success by convention; vendor does not document the type as boolean despite the semantics)
fields.errorObj: optional, type tns:Error -- { errorCode: string, errorDetails: string, errorMessage: string, errorNumber: double(nillable), errorType: string }

ErrorResponseShape.createIdLocation: SaveResult.id (double, nillable) -- the newly created record's ID on addRecipient/addGroup/editRecipient-style operations.

csvUploadMapping.where: uploadListQueue / uploadListQueueTest / UploadListInitialQueue request element -- maps CSV columns to MagnetMail's 42 custom recipient fields at bulk-upload time.

searchFilter.where: RecipientSearchCriteria (searchForRecipients filter fields) -- lowercase, no underscore, distinct casing/range from the upload-mapping convention above.

CustomObjectMarkerPattern.note: Not observed / not applicable. The WSDL exposes a fixed, vendor-defined operation and type surface with no customer-defined-object mechanism (no dynamic schema/describe operation for custom OBJECTS -- only custom FIELD slots on Recipients, see CustomFieldMarkerPattern).

WebhooksAvailable.note: Exhaustively enumerated all 55 operations in the WSDL portType; none registers a callback/webhook URL or subscription. Legacy ASP.NET .asmx web services of this vintage typically have no push/webhook mechanism.

BulkOperationsAvailable.mechanism: Async bulk-CSV upload job family: uploadListQueue / uploadListQueueTest / UploadListInitialQueue submit a CSV blob + MM_1..MM_42 column mapping and return a job id; getUploadJobStatus / getUploadJobStatusUTC / GetUploadInitialQueueJobStatus poll status. uploadSuppressionList is a separate bulk-suppress operation.
BulkOperationsAvailable.basePath: Same shared endpoint (mmapi.asmx) -- SOAP has no distinct REST-style base path; operations are distinguished by SOAPAction + body element, not URL.

APIVersioningStrategy.note: No version segment in the SOAP endpoint URL (/mmapi.asmx), the targetNamespace (http://www.magnetmail.net/), or any operation parameter. UTC-suffixed operation pairs (e.g. getMessages vs getMessagesUTC, getGroups vs getGroupsUTC) appear to be a timezone-handling variant, NOT an API version -- both members of each pair remain live in the current WSDL.

IncrementalSyncCapability.mechanism: Per-operation date-range parameters (naming varies -- see IncrementalWatermark). 11 of 55 operations expose a from/to date-range parameter pair; the remainder do not support incremental filtering at the API level.

WriteCapability.note: Confirmed by exhaustive operation-name scan (55 ops, zero name collisions on delete/remove/update -- the update verb here is "edit", not "update"). No delete/remove operation exists anywhere in the WSDL-enumerated surface.

Unsubscribes.create: unsubscribeRecipients (marks recipients unsubscribed -- a write, not a delete)

UploadJobs.create: uploadListQueue / uploadListQueueTest / UploadListInitialQueue (async bulk job submission)

Configuration.ConcurrencyControlNote: No ETag / version / rowversion / If-Match-style field found anywhere in the WSDL type system. Group carries last_updated_date/last_updated_loginid, but these are audit-trail OUTPUT fields only -- they are never accepted back as an input precondition on editRecipient/editMagnetMailMessage, so there is no compare-and-swap mechanism. Writes are unconditional overwrites.
Configuration.DeleteSemanticsNote: Zero delete/remove operations exist in the 55-operation WSDL surface (grep-verified, case-insensitive, across the full portType). unsubscribeRecipients is a state-change WRITE (marks a recipient unsubscribed), not a delete -- the underlying Recipient record is never removed. Orphan-deletion / hard-delete sync is NOT SAFE for this vendor: there is no API-level way to delete a record at all, soft or hard.
Configuration.DefaultSyncDirectionNote: Recommended default for every new EntityMap regardless of the vendor's write capability -- bidirectional is opt-in only, per client-data-safety discipline, and requires sandbox validation first.
Configuration.DefaultConflictResolutionNote: Left UNSET. With ConcurrencyControl=none, MostRecent conflict resolution has no reliable timestamp precondition to arbitrate on for writes lacking a server-accepted precondition field; recommending a specific policy without a live-tenant validation would be a guess. See METADATA_REPORT for the exact preconditions before bidirectional could be turned on.
Configuration.DiscoveryIsAuthoritativeNote: The WSDL is a FIXED, versionless operation surface fetched once at build time (this run) -- it is not a live per-credential describe/list endpoint that a runtime DiscoverObjects/DiscoverFields call re-queries per tenant. Absence of an object/field on a later refresh proves nothing about whether it still exists for a given tenant. The connector's DiscoveryIsAuthoritative getter MUST stay at its BaseIntegrationConnector default (false) -- never override to true for this vendor -- so the comprehensive-refresh deactivation path never disables Declared IO/IOF rows on absence.
Configuration.universalPKNote: No single vendor-wide PK field name. Each object family uses its own integer/string identifier (recipient identified by mail_user_id/id in RecipientSearchCriteria; group_id on Groups; message_id implied by MessageId fields in the tracking criteria types; jobid-style identifiers on the upload-job family). Per-IOF IsPrimaryKey determination is the ioiof-extractor's job, using getById-style operation parameters and response id fields as the signal -- not asserted here.

OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.Reason: Fire-and-forget send RPC — not a syncable object/collection; no queryable record set to ingest.
Fire-and-forget group-send RPC — not a syncable object/collection; no queryable record set to ingest.

Value.decision: Not wired as FK to User. Kept wired nowhere on all 5 occurrences, for consistency.
Value.reason: user_id / UserId / MailUserId is the mmAuthHeader authenticated-account scope field (copied verbatim from AuthenticateResponse.AuthenticationResult.user_id and re-sent on every subsequent SOAP call's <mmAuthHeader>). The WSDL's only User-shaped read operation is getUserDetails(user_id) -> a SINGLE tns:User (the caller's OWN account profile) -- there is no getUsers (list) operation anywhere in the 55-operation WSDL. So this field is an auth-scope identifier, NOT a business reference to an enumerable User collection. Wiring it as RelatedIntegrationObjectID -> User would be the path-LMS / GrowthZone FK-over-guess trap (a field that merely resembles an FK pattern but has no target collection semantics). Left wired NOWHERE, consistently, across all 5 occurrences.
